target: Progress-bar 'lying' premise — simulated; premise correct, usual explanation wrong
reason: Variance alone does NOT produce the effect: with randomly varying item costs, naive linear extrapolation error decays smoothly as 1/sqrt(n) (14% at 5% done, 9% at 10%, 3% at 50%) — noisy early, no halfway cliff. NON-STATIONARITY does: if late work is heavier (finalize/index/flush), the estimator is BIASED and biased in ONE direction the whole way — -68% at 5%, -54% at 25%, -36% at halfway, -18% at 75%, -4% at 95%; negative = over-promises. So the bar does not lie until halfway then become honest; it lies in the same direction throughout, and halfway is where the lie drops below the annoyance threshold. Root cause: the estimator ASSUMES the middle looks like the beginning — it does not track the middle. CAVEAT: this is a simulation of estimator behaviour under an ASSUMED cost profile, NOT a measurement of real installers; it shows the mechanism is sufficient, not that real bars fail this way. Independent quantitative support for SCT's design goal ('data present != data trustworthy') without touching the unproven mechanism.

target: Item-bank method LOCKED: Option C, split inverted, gated on a 60-item pilot
reason: Hermes asked A/B/C + whether to tag difficulty. Answer required checking whether item COUNT is the binding constraint. IT IS NOT. MEASURED: 62 of 63 items in the current bank score exactly 1.00 in every arm; only LIT-12 varies. LOGIC 126/126, AUX 15/15, ARITH 12/12, TOOL 3/3 all at 100.0%. A ceiling item yields ZERO discordant pairs and McNemar is computed entirely from discordant pairs, so it contributes exactly zero information. Scaling 64->500 at the same difficulty yields ~492 items contributing nothing. SIMULATED (4000 reps/cell, paired McNemar n=500): item-difficulty SD from 0.0 to 1.4 moves power only 0.82->0.93 at p_base 0.95 and is flat or slightly NEGATIVE at lower p_base — because the paired design already differences item difficulty out. So difficulty tagging does NOT buy power (answer to Hermes q2: tag it for the secondary mixed model and reporting, but nobody may claim it as a power lever; raw item identity suffices for the pre-registered primary). THE REAL LEVER is intra-family correlation: templated clones share a skeleton, so DE = 1+(m-1)*ICC; at ICC=0.6 with 17 clones/family, 493 items behave like ~47 independent items — potentially LESS effective n than the existing 64-item bank, for 458 items of authoring. Fewer clones per family, more families: 8/family at ICC=0.2 gives n_eff~200. DECISION: Option C with the split INVERTED from Hermes's proposal — ~29 existing families x ~8 (not 12-17) + ~25-30 NEW families x ~8, total ~460-500 across ~55-60 families, difficulty target 70-85% baseline (NOT >=95%), family_id MANDATORY or ICC is uncomputable. GATED on a 60-item pilot (30 current-difficulty + 30 harder, 6 families x 10, 2 models spanning the band, 2 carriers, N=3, temp 0 = 720 trials vs 30,000 for the full run) which measures the two unknowns: real difficulty distribution and empirical family ICC. NOT CLAIMED: the ICC values are ASSUMED, demonstrating magnitude not measuring it; the empirical 0.063 from the current bank is uninterpretable at the ceiling (variance ~0.0002) and must not be cited as 'low'; the power figures assume independence and are therefore OPTIMISTIC under clustering.
